step1.title: The 60-Second Pause
step1.subtitle: Sometimes an urge can feel like something you need to act on right away. Let’s practice creating a little space before you respond.

step2.title: Let's Try a Scenario
step2.subtitle: Imagine you’ve just left your house.
step2.visual_line1: You lock the front door and walk toward your car.
step2.visual_line2: You notice the pull to turn around and check.

step3.subtitle: You notice an urge to turn around and check.
step3.question: What would you normally feel pulled to do?

step4.title: You Don’t Have to Answer It Yet.
step4.subtitle: For the next 60 seconds, we’re going to practice making a little space between the urge and your response.
step4.detail: The goal isn’t to make the thought disappear. It’s to notice the urge without immediately answering it.

prompts: Notice the urge as it appears.
You can feel the pull without answering it.
Take a gentle breath and observe.
The urge is just a sensation right now.
You don’t have to solve uncertainty right away.
Notice where you feel tension in your body.
Thoughts come and go like ripples on water.
Creating space between thought and action.
You are observing the urge, not obeying it.
Uncertainty can be uncomfortable, and that's okay.
Let the thought be there without engaging.
Notice the impulse to fix or check.
Stay curious about the sensation.
You are in control of your response.
Nothing needs to be settled this very second.
You’ve created space for over 45 seconds.
Just notice the urge without rushing to act.
Almost there — resting in the pause.
Stay present with this final breath.
You completed the pause.

step6.title: You Made Space.
step6.subtitle: The goal wasn't to make the urge disappear. It was to give yourself a moment before responding.
step6.question: What did you notice?

reflections.felt_urge: I felt an urge to respond
reflections.could_wait: I could wait without answering it right away

step7.title: Where the Pause Fits
step7.subtitle: OCD creates a strong pull to respond immediately to doubt.
step7.space_title: This is the space you just practiced.
step7.detail: A pause gives you a moment before automatically following that pull.

step8.title: Practice Transfer
step8.subtitle: Imagine you’ve just sent an important message.
step8.visual_line1: You press send and close the conversation.
step8.visual_thought: “Did I say something wrong? Maybe I should read it again.”
step8.visual_line2: The same pattern: Thought → Urge → Pause → Choice.

step9.title: An Urge is Not an Instruction.
step9.subtitle: You don’t have to answer every urge immediately. A little space can create a different starting point.
